headline: No all-source direction call yet
summary: The sources observe different populations, periods, and definitions. They are retained side by side to expose disagreement; they must not be averaged into an agent-activity index.

rows.reading: 30-day AI-bot index 72.4; -10.7% versus the preceding 30-day control window.
rows.crossSourceRead: Useful comparable within-source reading, but neither raw volume nor all agent activity.

rows.reading: 15% of AI requests classified as fetchers; AI requests +30% from January to May.
rows.sample: Fixed Fastly customer cohort; source-defined crawler/fetcher labels
rows.crossSourceRead: Fetcher share is more relevant than generic bot volume, but it is not comparable to Cloudflare's index.

rows.reading: 47.9% of commerce traffic identified as AI bots as of December 2025.
rows.sample: Akamai commerce traffic; source-defined AI bots include unwanted traffic
rows.crossSourceRead: Shows material nonhuman traffic in one vertical, not productive agent activity or a cross-network trend.

rows.reading: Enterprise AI/ML transactions +83% in calendar 2025 versus 2024.
rows.sample: Zscaler customer base and security-control plane
rows.crossSourceRead: Enterprise sample supports adoption relevance, but it does not isolate autonomous agent actions.

rows.reading: Long-running agentic tasks increasingly appear in Claude Code and Cowork sessions; artifact yield was reported for a sampled product period.
rows.crossSourceRead: Supports deeper workflows in one product sample; it is not a census of enterprise autonomy or inference volume.

rows.reading: 114,533 registered servers in the first automated snapshot.
rows.crossSourceRead: Shows available integration surfaces, not active production use or machine-action volume.
